text:
alex.w: Quick sync — FinData POC kickoff on Mon. They want doc Q&A + extractive summarization. Can we get a short capacity + budget estimate for the presales deck?

maria.g: Got it. Use-case details? avg prompt size, expected concurrency, success criteria?

alex.w: They said ~5k queries/day, avg input 300 tokens, avg output 150 tokens. Peak concurrency estimate ~40 concurrent requests during business hours. Timeline: 6 week POC, can tolerate a soft latency SLO (p50 < 150ms, p95 < 450ms). Need cost estimate for sales — budget asked for ~$10k but flexible. Also they'll run security questionnaire but not heavy.

maria.g: Nice. Basic calc: 5k q/day * 450 tokens = 2.25M tokens/day (~15.75M tokens/week). For a 6-week POC that's ~94.5M tokens total.

maria.g: For latency: if we serve a 13B open model quantized to 4-bit (typical presales choice) and leverage prefix caching for docs, we can hit p50/p95 targets with modest batching.

owen.k: GPU sizing estimate: assuming Llama-2-13B-4bit: A100-40GB can handle ~20-30 RPS of small-medium prompts with continuous batching and KV cache; H100 would do ~35-50 RPS. For 40 concurrent, recommend baseline 2x A100 (steady) with autoscale to 4x A100 for burst windows, or 1x H100 + 1x H100 warm for redundancy and burst to 2.

owen.k: If we prefer cost-savings and use smaller batch windows + more aggressive KV cache (docs prefix hit ~60%), effective throughput needs drop — so 2x A100 baseline still safe.

maria.g: Cost back-of-envelope (cloud/GPU only): A100-40GB equivalent infra ~ $2.5/hr per GPU (our dedicated pricing), H100 ~ $5/hr. For 2x A100 steady 24/7 for 6 weeks: 2 * $2.5 * 24 * 42 = $5,040. Burst headroom (avg half the time scale to 4 GPUs during business hours) add ~$2k.

maria.g: Redwood usage (tokens + service) — estimate token processing + bandwidth ~ $0.00012/token for this model/profile => 94.5M * $0.00012 = $11,340. That seems high; we should offer presales discount and cap.

jess.l: For POC success criteria we recommend a short list for FinData to sign off: 1) Functional: 90% accuracy on 20 eval prompts (they'll provide labeled Q&A). 2) Performance: p95 latency < 450ms under 40 concurrent for 80% of test window. 3) Cost: projected monthly run-rate for production under target traffic < $X (we'll provide range). 4) Security: private VPC connectivity verified in staging.

alex.w: Can we tighten the token estimate? They mentioned lots of long documents and potential chunking. If prefix cache hit is higher (80%) that reduces tokens by ~30%.

owen.k: Right — caching, chunk size, and whether they use retrieval-augmented generation will change numbers. If RAG reduces model calls by 40% (local matches), tokens drop to ~56.7M for 6 weeks. That reduces Redwood usage to ~$6.8k.

maria.g: Updated cost scenarios for deck: 
- Conservative (no caching, steady 2x A100 + bursts): infra ~$7k + usage ~$11.3k => total ~$18.3k for POC period.
- Likely (60% cache hit, 2x A100 baseline): infra ~$5k + usage ~$6.8k => total ~$11.8k.
- Optimistic (80% cache, RAG reduces calls 40%, 1x H100 baseline): infra ~$3.5k + usage ~$4k => total ~$7.5k.

maria.g: We should offer to include a token cap and an autoscale budget cap for the POC to protect pricing. Recommend a $12k cap with alerts.

presales-bot: PRESALES CHECKLIST: confirm eval prompts (20), provide sample docs (5), SLA window for tests, whitelist IPs, decide on VPC vs hosted.

jess.l: Also need to lock model variant for repeatable evals and record seeds for deterministic sampling in tests.

alex.w: Can someone draft 1-slide summary and a short email to FinData with the 3 cost scenarios + recommended cap? Meeting with them Wed 10am.

maria.g: I'll do the slide + scenario table and include GPU/RUN assumptions.

owen.k: I'll post a short config snippet for the POC deployment (autoscale rules + cache settings).

deploy-bot: deploy plan snippet: 
```
model: llama-2-13b-4bit
baseline_gpus: 2x A100
autoscale: min=2 max=4 cpu_threshold=65% queue_latency_slo=0.45
cache: prefix_kv ttl=24h expected_hit=0.6
token_cap: 12_000_000
```

alex.w: Perfect. Maria — can you drop the slide in #sales by EOD? I'll review before Wed. :thumbsup:

maria.g: Yep, will upload by 5pm PST.

alex.w: Thanks team — will prep presales email after your slides.
